sections.label: Not the troubled teen industry
sections.heading: Not the troubled teen industry
sections.body:
The industries on these pages are not part of the troubled teen industry, and Kids Over Profits does not track their facilities. They are here because they connect to it in four ways.

They share its roots. Our [history timelines](/history/) trace how orphanages and orphan trains, institutions for disabled children and the eugenics movement shaped the first troubled teen programs, and the teen program itself began as a psychiatric idea.

They share its owners. The same companies and private equity investors have run psychiatric hospitals, foster care, adult group homes and nursing homes alongside teen programs.

They share its methods. The behavior control used on teenagers was developed on disabled children and in psychiatric wards, and the same restraint has killed people in psychiatric hospitals, group homes and youth programs.

They share its children. States place children from foster care in the programs we track, and disabled children can grow up inside companies that run both.

We are not the experts on these industries. Each page points to the people and organizations who are.

sections.label: The pages
sections.heading: Industries connected to the troubled teen industry
sections.body:
- [Foster care](/foster-care/): States place children in their custody in the residential programs we track, run by the same companies, where children have been restrained to death and abused.
- [Group homes for adults with developmental disabilities](/disability-group-homes/): They grew from the same institutions as the troubled teen industry, some of the same companies run both, and its methods of behavior control were developed on disabled children.
- [Nursing homes](/nursing-homes/): Children were moved out of the almshouses they shared with old and disabled people, and some of the same private equity investors have owned nursing homes and teen programs.
- [Psychiatric hospitals and psych wards](/psychiatric-hospitals/): The teen program grew out of the psychiatric hospital, and the same chains own both and run them the same way: people who cannot leave are kept to fill beds and held down.

sections.label: What we count as the troubled teen industry
sections.heading: What we do count as the troubled teen industry
sections.body:
Residential treatment centers, psychiatric residential treatment facilities for young people, therapeutic boarding schools, wilderness programs, shelters for migrant children and juvenile detention are all part of what we track. You will find them in our [program directory](/tti-program-index/). Programs for [young adults over 18](/young-adult-programs/) are kept in their own list, but they are part of the industry too.

The [Indian boarding schools and residential schools](/indian-boarding-schools/) of the United States and Canada are not an industry and are not on these pages. They have a page of their own.

sections.label: Tell us if we got this wrong
sections.heading: Tell us if we got this wrong
sections.body: If you work in one of these fields, or have lived in one of these places, and something on these pages is wrong, please [tell us](/contact/). We will change it.
